title: The Minotaur
subtitle: Following the thread's guidance, she finds the way out.

trails.title: Same as Before
trails.description: The world is changing so quickly that even a tortoise has to pick up the pace.

content.text:
After discussions at the headquarters and based on the current global situation and the conditions of each branch, the following transfer notices are officially announced:

The Texas base will be abandoned and all personnel evacuated.

Comrade Igor will be transferred to the Zeno-Brazil branch to succeed General Carlos as commander.

All other branches will remain unchanged.

This transfer notice is official and has been approved by the Pax Security Council, effective immediately.

1990.9.22

items.text: The Minotaur
Meeting Room

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Lieutenant Moldir, about time. What was it? Did you stop for a picnic?
A scalding comment.
Moldir was supposed to be taking care of Ms. Sotheby. It seems she has abandoned her duties.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Admiral, I ...

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Save your excuses.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Yes, sir!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: It was my fault, Admiral. I ran into her on our way here. It's been a while since we last saw each other.
As her father glares at her, she quickly realizes that her attempt to cover for her sister is only making things worse.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Your performance on the training ground earlier was most impressive, Ms. Lopera.
She breaks the awkward silence.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Allow me to introduce my team. This is Ms. Sotheby.
Sotheby smiles and curtsies.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And this is Lieutenant Lilya.
She gives a brief salute.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: How's it going? I was previously assigned to HQ.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: It seems your assignment here has done little for your discipline, Lopera.
The admiral stands with his hands behind his back. He examines his undisciplined daughter, a grim look on his face.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: You have new orders. I am assigning you to accompany the Timekeeper and her team to São Paulo for the duration of their mission.
Lopera nods, but Lilya still has questions.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Me and Lopera? That's a whole lot of firepower. What are we expecting during this mission?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Oh! Sorry, Lilya. I haven't had the chance to speak with you privately. The Admiral asked if you could stay on site to help with training their new recruits.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What do you think? You can do as you wish.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Training up some new blood, eh? Well, as long as you think you can handle things without me, I can stick around to lend a hand. It'll be just like the good old days back at the academy.
She knows that this isn't a request but an order.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Thank you, Lieutenant.
He nods and smiles in thanks. His smile fades as he turns to his youngest daughter.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: As for you, Lopera ...

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Please show our guests to their rooms, and try not to over-exert yourself.
Orders have been given to everyone present.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Lieutenant Lilya, stay for a moment.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Lieutenant Moldir will bring some documents shortly; they should prove useful for your assignment.
Moldir, briefly out of the admiral's sight, shrugs helplessly as her orders start to pile up.
Lilya gives her a knowing smile. It's always like this. It's just part of the job.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Now, I have other business to attend to. If you'll excuse me.
He turns and leaves, his imposing figure soon disappearing from sight.
Lopera exhales a long breath, snaps her fingers, and smiles as she heads toward the door. She turns to her guests.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Come on, let's go. I'll show you around. But stay close. This base can be a bit of a labyrinth. It's only missing a bloodthirsty minotaur lurking its halls. Well, I haven't seen him yet, anyways.
Zeno Base

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: The base here has been understaffed for some time; whole sections are deserted—it can be dangerous. We don't usually allow guests to move about freely.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Well, who am I kidding? We don't have any guests in the first place. Who'd come here for a visit?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: "Scenic views of dead gardens and overgrown brush. In the spring we have vine-tripping competitions, and in the summer you can be part of our complementary bug buffet!"

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Even the farmers back home had it better than this.
She leads the way, chewing on a piece of wolf's-tail grass.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Before Zeno moved in, this was the fort of some Lisbon aristocrat.
The shadows of the old continent are everywhere here, the ghosts of the 18th century still clinging to every mark on the marble columns.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: There's only one place fully off-limits here: that tower.
She points to a tower in the distance.
Styled after Andalusian architecture, it stands ominously under the scorching sun, looming over the base with an eerie intensity.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's in there?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: It must be the minotaur's lair!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Or a secret lab for super soldiers!
Sotheby's imagination is running wild again.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Imbued with the strength of an ox, the wits of a man, and the wings and fiery breath of a dragon!

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Miss, this is a Zeno base, not some chimera's nest.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Besides, if there were any monsters in there, I would have heard them by now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Were those the Admiral's exact words? That nobody is allowed "inside" the tower?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Yeah, that was what he said: "Under no circumstances is anyone to be allowed inside."
Then a quick peek around wouldn't exactly violate the letter of that order.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ms. Vertin, are you thinking what I'm thinking?
Is there treasure inside the tower?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Let me say this again: There are no monsters in that tower.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: And I am under orders to escort you directly to your rooms.
She blinks. Clearly, curiosity isn't only in the hearts of these new guests.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: But if we were to, say, walk a bit too close, and "accidentally" provoke some nearby critters ...
Mischievous critters often wander into the courtyards, and these ones have appeared just in time.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh! How terrible! It seems trouble has found us!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: They gave me quite a start! Thankfully, they were easy to handle.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: We can't let them run off. Who knows what damage they could do?
Lopera chases after the fleeing critters, who just so happen to be heading in the direction of the tower.
It is nothing more than a coincidence.
The half-hour-long game of "tag" finally comes to an end.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Now where could they have gone?
She searches for the colorful critters, a serious look on her face. In her concentration, she bumps into a wooden door flanked by lemon trees.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It may well be possible they fled into the tower.
The door stands at the base of the tower.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is this the entrance?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Timekeeper!
Clearly, this door is not supposed to be opened.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: My father, the admiral, he won't be happy with this.
The sight of it is tantalizing. Just a touch, and it will swing open, revealing all the mysteries within.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: But why? Is there something hidden inside?
Claw marks line the wall, and blood stains the door—rabbit blood, bull blood, unblessed lamb blood.
The wind stirs the lemon trees, filling the air with the faint scent of bay and myrtle.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's an arcane array on the door.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is it to stop us from entering, or to keep what's inside from coming out?
The arcane array looks ancient. It has weakened with time.
She traces the markings with her fingertips. The blood flakes off, breaking a small gap in the array.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: I have no idea. We're soldiers, we "follow orders, no questions." As my father would say.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: With all the flooding we've had, they probably shoved everything they wanted to keep safe and dry in there.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Lopera!
Moldir rushes from behind, putting an end to their little "accidental" adventure.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: You get lost on your way to the guest rooms, Pera? You know better than to be here.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Your ship will be leaving early tomorrow morning. Please return to your rooms and get some rest.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: This is a military base, not an amusement park. Please, do not wander about, especially near restricted areas.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: My apologies, Lieutenant. Perhaps you could point us in the right direction?
She steals one more look at the tower as they leave. The fruits on the lemon trees are plump and juicy. The old beast-blood array appears dark in the sunlight.
The wooden door creaks open a little, allowing an insect to fly in through the gap.
The seal ... it's gone.
Inside the tower, the sole prisoner has been quietly listening to their conversation: There's a ship leaving tomorrow morning.
As the footsteps trail off, she gently pushes the door. The seal is indeed gone. She's free.
TO BE CONTINUED…
